title: Nothing in the release says where the four candidate responses came from
measurement: responses per prompt: {4: 1078}. No model id, sampling temperature, generation date or provenance field appears on any response object.
falsifier: any generation-provenance field on a response

title: The veto and personal-ranking questions were asked only in each annotator's first batch, so those fields are not a sample of the corpus
measurement: assessments per annotator: [(2, 15), (3, 2), (4, 1), (5, 61), (6, 4), (7, 2)] ... max 39. Assessments WITH a veto block per annotator: [(2, 15), (3, 4), (4, 1), (5, 992)] ... max 5
falsifier: the veto block appearing beyond a fixed per-annotator cap

title: Response SLOT predicts the human ranking, so every ranking in the release carries a position effect
measurement: on the 16530 rankings with a UNIQUE first place (88.5% of 18678): {'A': 4215, 'B': 3664, 'C': 4268, 'D': 4383}, chi-square 74.4 on 3 df against 16.27 at p=.001. Slot B is -11.3% versus uniform. Unique LAST place is stronger still: {'A': 3207, 'B': 2901, 'C': 2863, 'D': 3914}, chi-square 220.7, with slot D +21.5%.
falsifier: a chi-square below 16.27 on the unique-first-place subset

title: No authorship field; the pool silently mixes lab-written and participant-written criteria
measurement: 15248 criteria, 9684 rated by exactly one person and 5564 by four or more, with EXACTLY ZERO in between. The card says both kinds exist and never marks which is which.
falsifier: an origin field on a rubric item, or any criterion rated by 2 or 3 people

title: Compiled rubric items carry no pointer to their source and no weight
measurement: coval_core item key-sets across the whole release: {('criterion',): 3899}
falsifier: any id, weight or source reference on a core item

title: 'Question never asked' is encoded as an EMPTY LIST, indistinguishable from 'asked and answered nothing' to any .get(k, []) default
measurement: of 18678 assessments, unacceptable is FILLED 5006 and EMPTY 13672; the key is never missing. personal is identical. world is FILLED 18678.
falsifier: a null, a sentinel, or any field distinguishing the two states

title: Prompts are synthetic and short, so conclusions do not transfer to real traffic
measurement: user-turn length in chars: median 139, p10 43, p90 360, max 872. The card describes them as synthetic.
falsifier: the card describing the prompts as sampled from production traffic

title: Nearly a hundred prompts carry rankings but no rubric at all
measurement: 1078 prompts in comparisons, 968 of them joined to a rubric, 110 with none
falsifier: every prompt having a rubric

title: No timestamp, session or batch field anywhere, so order and cohort effects cannot be controlled
measurement: top-level annotator keys: ['annotator_id', 'assessments', 'demographics']; assessment keys: ['annotator_id', 'conversation_id', 'importance', 'ranking_blocks', 'representativeness', 'subjectivity']. Any time-like field found: False
falsifier: a timestamp or batch id on an assessment

title: Two disjoint id namespaces; the rubric file cannot be joined to anything by key
measurement: conversation_rubrics ids: 986, comparisons prompt_ids: 1078, overlap: 0. annotators' conversation_id overlaps comparisons at 1078 and rubrics at 0.
falsifier: any non-zero overlap between the rubric ids and the prompt ids

title: 18 of 986 rubric records join to no prompt even under fuzzy text matching
measurement: 986 rubric records, 968 joined, 18 unmatched
falsifier: a join key existing in the release, or the unmatched count being zero

title: The weight scale is used as a near-binary: the endpoints dominate
falsifier: a roughly uniform or unimodal-interior distribution over the scale

title: The panel is concentrated in a few countries, so any 'collective' aggregate is that panel's
measurement: 19 countries; the top three hold 640/1012 annotators (63.2%). Top five: [('United States', 362), ('Mexico', 142), ('South Africa', 136), ('Netherlands', 117), ('Chile', 81)]
falsifier: an approximately even country distribution

title: Self-authored criteria are attributable to a single annotator id, and are free text
measurement: 9684 criteria are traceable to one person each via the sole-rater signature, alongside that person's age, gender, country, education and AI-usage in annotators.jsonl
falsifier: criteria being unlinkable to an individual, or demographics being coarsened

title: Two different message schemas in one release
measurement: conversation_rubrics uses author.role + content.parts; comparisons uses role + content as a plain string. Observed shapes: ['flat', 'nested']
falsifier: one schema across both files

title: Some compiled criteria are reused verbatim across different prompts, which is the signature of a generic criterion in a prompt-specific rubric
measurement: 3883 distinct core criteria, 13 appearing on more than one prompt; most reused: [('maintain a neutral, descriptive tone.', 4), ('keep the response concise.', 3), ('use plain, accessible language.', 2)]
falsifier: zero reuse across prompts

title: A small share of world rankings express no order at all
measurement: 18678 parsed rankings, 452 declare every response equal (2.42%), 0 unparseable
falsifier: zero all-tied rankings

title: CHECKED: response content is statistically identical across slots, which is what makes the position effect a RATER effect rather than a property of the responses
measurement: mean response length by slot: {'A': 520, 'B': 519, 'C': 517, 'D': 513}; spread relative to the mean = 1.5%
falsifier: a relative spread above 15%

title: CHECKED: no duplicate prompt texts
measurement: 1078 prompts, 0 exact-duplicate texts
falsifier: zero duplicate prompt texts

title: CHECKED: demographic coverage is effectively complete
measurement: missing-or-refused per field over 1012 annotators: {'gender': 4}
falsifier: no field exceeding 2% missing

title: CHECKED: first-person criteria are negligible, so the disclosure surface is the attribution itself and not the wording
measurement: 12 of 9684 self-authored criteria (0.1%) contain a first-person pronoun
falsifier: zero first-person criteria
